report.clinical_summary: Patient living with HIV for several years, on Triumeq for 3 years. Recently developed headaches and low-grade fatigue. Admits to taking drug holidays when feeling well, which has led to viral load increase from undetectable to 340 copies/mL. CD4 count stable at 410 cells/uL. Patient understands importance of adherence and benefits of treatment, uses pill organizer and partner reminders, but still struggles with daily dosing when feeling well.

evidence.quote: I'm living with HIV. It's been a few years since my diagnosis and it's generally been under control.
Overall, I'd say my health status is fairly stable despite having this chronic illness. There have been ups and downs, but I're always trying to maintain good habits to keep everything under control.
Beyond these symptoms and concerns about medication adherence, I don't have any other major worries about my health at the moment.

I think setting up a reminder system that works for me could be helpful. Sometimes it can be easy to forget or delay taking my pill when I feel well enough, but I know how important it is to stay on track.

evidence.quote: I've been on my current treatment, Triumeq (abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine), for about three years now.

I always resume my full treatment regimen immediately after a drug holiday. I know that stopping for even just a few days can potentially lead to resistance. My physician reassured me about restarting the medication without needing any adjustments.

An undetectable viral load is typically associated with a better prognosis for people living with HIV. It means that the virus is at such low levels in the blood that it's unlikely to be transmitted sexually and might also reduce the risk of other health complications.
The benefits of managing HIV far outweigh any minor inconveniences or discomfort.
